extraction_warnings: This paper reports aggregate, group-level (subgroup) data for three groups (control, pHTN, HTN) rather than individual sample-level records; several schema fields intended for per-sample metadata (subject_id, sample_id, ncbi_accession, age, sex) are not available in the main text.
Detailed demographic and clinical data (age, sex, BMI, etc.) are referenced as being in Additional file 1: Table S1, which was not included in the provided paper text.
PMID was inferred from the paper_id field rather than found explicitly stated in the text.
Sequencing platform model (HiSeq) is confirmed only for 16S rRNA sequencing of mouse samples; shotgun metagenomic sequencing platform model is not explicitly specified beyond 'Illumina platform'.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy control', 'Pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'Hypertension (HTN)'] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'hypertension (HTN)']; kept batch 0.
Age and BMI were mentioned as compared clinical variables (Additional file 1: Table S1) but exact numeric values were not present in the provided text.
FMT donor/recipient identifiers exist in Additional file 11: Table S17 but were not included in the provided text.
Smoker status was inferred from an exclusion criterion rather than directly stated as a smoking status label.

Granularity was set to subgroup_level primarily due to the disease/disease_details fields; several other fields (e.g., antibiotics_current_use) apply uniformly to the whole cohort rather than being subgroup-specific.
Batch 2 subgroups ['Control', 'pHTN', 'HTN'] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'hypertension (HTN)']; kept batch 0.
This schema appears designed for oncology/clinical trial studies (ECOG, tumor size, OS); most such fields are not applicable to this gut microbiota-hypertension study and were marked not_reported.

The study involves two host species (human participants and germ-free mice for FMT), but the schema only allows a single host_species value; human was selected as primary since mice were experimental recipients, not the main study cohort.

biomarker_name/value/unit fields were populated using blood pressure classification thresholds (SBP/DBP) as the closest matching quantifiable clinical parameters reported in the paper; these represent group-defining criteria rather than per-patient continuous measurements.

feces_phenotype_value could not be confidently mapped to a specific reported value given the schema's generic/ambiguous description; the paper contains extensive but unstructured microbial abundance data.
